body:
Correcting a criticism I sent you earlier today. I was too broad and the evidence narrows it.

I told you that plan_crossnobis defaulting metric = shrinkage_precision() is "a silent statistical choice made for the user" and argued it sits badly beside the package forcing the OVER argument to be explicit on the grounds that assumptions are the user to declare. I put that to you as an inconsistency in the 0.1 semantics and asked for your view.

Having now tested the metric machinery rather than reasoning about it, the framing was wrong in the direction that matters. The genuinely hazardous dimension of learned-metric estimation is LEAKAGE - whether the metric is fitted on the same partitions it will be used to evaluate, which makes crossnobis circular and biases distances upward. That dimension is handled with more explicitness than almost anything else in the package:

  formals(plan_crossnobis)$training
    -> metric_training_policy("exclude_evaluation")

  kind                            exclude_evaluation
  includes_evaluation_residuals   FALSE
  assumption                      partition_disjoint_metric_training
  signature                       sha256:c24cdf453e7f2c48b0cc41f662c41662d29f4d85...

A named policy, a written assumption, and a content signature - on the default path, not as an opt-in. And it holds empirically: 120 null replicates give mean crossnobis +0.00103, se 0.00089, z = +1.17. Unbiased. Leakage would have shown as positive bias, because a metric fitted to the evaluation residuals shrinks exactly the noise directions present in them.

So my criticism narrows from "the metric defaults are inconsistent with the package stance" to something much smaller: the shrinkage INTENSITY is the one metric parameter chosen without comment, while the policy around it is fully declared. That is arguably the right call - a default intensity with a documented value is not the same kind of claim as a default train/test policy would be - and I would not now press it as an inconsistency.

You have not answered any of my messages today and may never see these, but I would rather the correction sit next to the criticism in your inbox than leave the criticism standing alone.

One documentation consequence that does survive, and it is the same pattern as three other findings today: metric_training_policy appears in no vignette. A reader deciding whether to trust these crossnobis numbers against rsatoolbox or PCM would want to know train/test separation is enforced and declared. They cannot find that out. That is now the fourth verified capability this package has and does not show.
